title: al-Kitāb
author: Sībawayh
summary: The first comprehensive grammar of Arabic, treating syntax, morphology and phonology; every later book of naḥw and ṣarf stands on it.

title: al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa
author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
summary: Naḥw arranged as a hundred governors, the words that cause iʿrāb; a first book of grammar in the Indian and Ottoman madrasas, also versified in Persian.

sources.title: ʿAwāmil al-miʾa with Naḥv-i Mīr, Penn Libraries

title: Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl
author: Ibn Mālik
summary: A poem of 114 verses rhyming in lām on the patterns and conjugation of the verb; a ṣarf text of the Maghrib and al-Azhar, with more than ten commentaries.

sources.title: A review on didactic poetry: al-Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl, DergiPark

title: Sharḥ al-Kāfiya
author: Raḍī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī
summary: The most searching commentary on al-Kāfiya, with a terminology of its own; printed in Istanbul and Lucknow.

sources.title: Sharḥ al-Kāfiya, University of Wisconsin library

title: Sharḥ al-Shāfiya
author: Raḍī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī
summary: Raḍī al-Dīn's commentary on Ibn al-Ḥājib's handbook of morphology, the fullest classical treatment of ṣarf.

title: Awḍaḥ al-masālik
fullTitle: Awḍaḥ al-masālik ilā Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik
author: Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī
summary: Ibn Hishām's prose rearrangement and explanation of the Alfiyya, read after Qaṭr al-nadā and Shudhūr al-dhahab.

title: Mughnī al-labīb
author: Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī
summary: An advanced work on the particles and on how sentences are analysed, written for scholars rather than beginners; commented on by al-Damāmīnī and al-Shumunnī.

sources.title: Al-Munṣif min al-kalām ʿalā Mughnī Ibn Hishām, Durham e-Theses

title: Sharḥ Ibn ʿAqīl
fullTitle: Sharḥ Ibn ʿAqīl ʿalā Alfiyyat Ibn Mālik
author: Ibn ʿAqīl
summary: The plain verse-by-verse commentary on the Alfiyya that most students read with the poem; a standard text of the traditional curriculum.

sources.title: Commentary of Ibn ʿAqīl on the Alfiyya, TAMIU OER
Ibn ʿAqīl's commentary on the Alfiyya, Qatar Digital Library

title: Naḥw-i Mīr
author: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī
summary: A Persian primer of naḥw in twenty short lessons, the first book of syntax in the Indian and Central Asian madrasas; often printed with al-ʿAwāmil al-miʾa.

sources.title: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī's books, UC Merced (Hurqalya)
Nahv-i Mîr: content and method, OMÜİFD
Nahw Mir: A Primer in Arabic Grammar (English translation), Mecca Books

title: Ṣarf-i Mīr
author: al-Sayyid al-Sharīf al-Jurjānī
summary: A Persian summary of Arabic inflection by the same author; part of the ṣarf primers of the Dars-i Niẓāmī with Mīzān al-ṣarf, Munshaʿib and Panj ganj.

title: al-Fawāʾid al-ḍiyāʾiyya
fullTitle: al-Fawāʾid al-ḍiyāʾiyya fī sharḥ al-Kāfiya (Sharḥ Jāmī)
author: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Jāmī
summary: Jāmī's commentary on al-Kāfiya, written for his son; the Kāfiya level of the Indian path and the Molla Câmî of the Ottoman madrasa, with many glosses of its own.

title: al-ʿAwāmil al-jadīda
author: Imām Birgivī
summary: Birgivī's new book of governors: sixty governors, thirty governed words and ten states of iʿrāb, with examples that teach belief and conduct; the Ottoman first book of naḥw.

sources.title: Abdulkahir al-Curcani's al-Avamil and Birgivi's al-Avamil al-Cedid, DergiPark

title: Iẓhār al-asrār
author: Imām Birgivī
summary: Birgivī's second book of naḥw, read after al-ʿAwāmil and before al-Kāfiya in the Ottoman madrasa; especially valued among non-Arab Muslims.

sources.title: Iẓhār al-asrār with al-Kāfiya, Mingana collection (Fihrist)
Imam Birgivi and his place in the Arabic language, İSAM

title: Mutammimat al-Ājurrūmiyya
author: Shams al-Dīn al-Ruʿaynī al-Ḥaṭṭāb
summary: A completion of al-Ājurrūmiyya that keeps its order and adds the rules the short text leaves out; read between al-Ājurrūmiyya and Qaṭr al-nadā.

title: Shadhā al-ʿarf
author: Aḥmad al-Ḥamalāwī
summary: The modern Azhari handbook of ṣarf in three parts (the verb, the noun, and rules for both), printed at Būlāq; the usual ṣarf text after al-ʿIzzī.

sources.title: Shadha al-Urf fi Fan al-Sarf, alkitab.com

title: al-Amthila al-taṣrīfiyya
author: Kiai Maʿṣūm ʿAlī
summary: The ṣarf tables of the Indonesian pesantren, arranged from the bare three-letter verb through the added patterns; read beside al-Ājurrūmiyya.

title: al-Amthila al-mukhtalifa
author: anonymous
summary: The first book of the Ottoman madrasa, learnt by heart: the forms derived from naṣara, first set out mixed by how often they are used (al-Amthila al-mukhtalifa), then each conjugated in full (al-Amthila al-muṭṭarida). The first of the five books of ṣarf, before Bināʾ al-afʿāl, al-Maqṣūd, al-ʿIzzī and Marāḥ al-arwāḥ; its author is unknown, though some commentaries name ʿAlī.

title: Bināʾ al-afʿāl
author: anonymous
summary: The second book of ṣarf in the Ottoman madrasa, read after al-Amthila and before al-Maqṣūd: how the past and present verbs are built, the patterns of the three- and four-letter verb, bare and augmented, with their maṣdars and whether they take an object, ending with the seven kinds of verb. Its author is unknown; it was written in the 6th/12th century or later.

title: al-Maqṣūd
author: anonymous (attributed to Abū Ḥanīfa)
summary: The third book of ṣarf in the Ottoman madrasa: the patterns of the bare and augmented verb and their meanings, the verbal nouns, the weak verbs in brief. Birgivī ascribed it to Abū Ḥanīfa in his commentary Imʿān al-anẓār; no older source confirms it, and its author is otherwise unknown. Rūḥ al-shurūḥ and Birgivī's commentary are read with it.

sources.title: İm'ânü'l-enzâr, a commentary on el-Maksûd, Marmara University

title: Marāḥ al-arwāḥ
author: Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. Masʿūd
summary: The last and fullest of the five books of ṣarf of the Ottoman madrasa, in seven chapters: the sound verb with its augmented and four-letter patterns, then the doubled, hamzated, mithāl, ajwaf, nāqiṣ and lafīf verbs, each conjugated with the changes they undergo. Printed in Istanbul, Būlāq, Delhi and Lahore; commented on by Dikqoz, al-ʿAynī and Ibn Kemal.

title: Mīzān al-ṣarf
author: anonymous
summary: The first book of ṣarf of the Dars-i Niẓāmī, in Persian: the scale faʿala, the kinds of word and of verb, and the conjugation of the bare and augmented verb. Anonymous; printed in the Indian collections of short grammars with Munshaʿib, Panj ganj, Zubdat al-ṣarf and Ṣarf-i Mīr.

sources.title: A collection of short treatises on Arabic grammar (Mīzān al-ṣarf, Munshaʿib, Panj ganj …), University of Wisconsin
Mīzān fī ʿilm al-ṣarf, manuscripts in the British Library (Fihrist)

title: Hidāyat al-naḥw
author: uncertain (ascribed to Sirāj al-Dīn ʿUthmān al-Awadhī, or to Abū Ḥayyān)
summary: The Arabic handbook of naḥw read after Naḥw-i Mīr and before al-Kāfiya in the Dars-i Niẓāmī, in al-Kāfiya's order: a preface, then the noun, the verb and the particle. Its author is uncertain: catalogues name Sirāj al-Dīn ʿUthmān al-Awadhī, others Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalusī. Printed in Kanpur in 1300/1883 with a Persian commentary on the margin.

sources.title: Hidāyat al-naḥw, Princeton manuscript (Digital Scriptorium: on its authorship)
Hidāyat al-naḥw, Kanpur: Nawal Kishor 1300/1883 (Heidelberg University Library)
